bullets: Macro forecasting is mostly humility plus a few dependable signals rather than elaborate prediction — a pattern observed at teams using BloombergNEF and IPCC and seen holding across three different teams.
Reliability of data trumps cleverness of model; the framing matters because it reveals which trade-offs a forecaster is actually making.
Second-order effects are the part of macroeconomics most people miss — first-order reasoning alone leaves the most consequential dynamics unexamined.
Trade-offs around reliability cross-cut every other aspect of risk management and macroeconomics rather than sitting in a single isolated domain.
Practical adoption starts small — pick one idea, run it for two weeks, and treat everything after that as iteration rather than a one-time overhaul.
